editorial_thesis: Prefer a small, testable control or data-boundary improvement over another generic model roundup.

topic_groups.title: Agent Platform Operations
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh Aug 14–15 release-note signal shows the agent stack moving from model choice to durable workspaces, governed collaboration surfaces, and platform migration hygiene.

sources.title: Vertex AI becomes Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
sources.why_selected: Google’s own release notes now point readers to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform as the current home for Vertex AI services.
sources.usefulness: Audit any Buildn/client architecture references that still assume Vertex AI is the stable product boundary.

sources.title: Workspace Chat and Sheets/Slides MCP capabilities
sources.why_selected: Workspace release notes expose richer Chat search/events and developer-preview MCP servers for Sheets and Slides.
sources.usefulness: Prototype an agent that reads a brief, updates a planning sheet, and leaves an auditable Chat trace.

sources.title: ChatGPT project-only memory and Linux preview
sources.why_selected: Project-only memory is now configurable, while ChatGPT and Codex are in public preview on major Linux distributions.
sources.usefulness: Use project-only memory as a clean boundary for client dossiers and test Linux-native operator workflows.

sources.title: Visual Studio 2026 release notes
sources.why_selected: Microsoft’s 2026 release line positions AI integration alongside performance and platform fundamentals.
sources.usefulness: Compare its agent ergonomics with the tools used in client engineering handoffs.

sources.title: Google ADK long-running agents
sources.why_selected: The durable pattern remains operationally relevant: pause, resume, and checkpoint long-running work instead of relying on chat history.
sources.usefulness: Reuse the pattern for research and publishing jobs that can survive retries or approvals.

topic_groups.title: Agent Security Control Plane
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Security coverage is under-rotated in the recent archive, while fresh Cisco and current research make the practical control surface unusually concrete: inventory, inline checks, accountability, and revocation.

sources.title: Cisco AI Defense 2026.8.1
sources.why_selected: Cisco added project-scoped AI asset management and native LiteLLM guardrails with fail-closed behavior and structured decision logs.
sources.usefulness: Use project ownership plus inline prompt/tool inspection as a reference architecture for governed agent delivery.

sources.title: State of AI Agent Security 2026
sources.why_selected: A 750-person survey reports fleets doubling while roughly 48% of production agents remain unsecured or unmonitored.
sources.usefulness: Turn the confidence-versus-coverage gap into a client discovery question and an agent inventory metric.

sources.title: AI Security Report 2026
sources.why_selected: Check Point frames AI as an active operator inside live intrusions, not merely a development aid.
sources.usefulness: Use the report to broaden threat modeling from prompt injection to AI-assisted attacker workflows.

sources.title: AI agent identity governance gap
sources.why_selected: CSA research highlights missing visibility into agent identities and weak confidence in governance readiness.
sources.usefulness: Make agent owner, delegated authority, expiry, and revocation mandatory fields in delivery artifacts.

sources.title: NIST software and AI-agent adoption concept paper
sources.why_selected: NIST’s concept paper gives a standards-oriented frame for accelerating adoption without treating agents as ordinary software components.
sources.usefulness: Use it as a neutral reference when clients need governance language beyond vendor claims.

topic_groups.title: Local-First Knowledge Operations
topic_groups.selection_rationale: After several cloud-agent days, this lane deliberately tests the neglected practical alternative: owned data, sync reliability, and self-hosted observability for knowledge-heavy workflows.

sources.title: Obsidian LiveSync releases
sources.why_selected: Recent fixes address remote configuration and local database access during sync setup, a small but meaningful reliability signal for private knowledge systems.
sources.usefulness: Use it to test a local-first research notebook with a separately controlled sync backend.

sources.title: NocoDB releases
sources.why_selected: NocoDB’s release stream calls out self-hosting notes and clearer boundaries around SQLite as an external data source.
sources.usefulness: Evaluate it as a lightweight, inspectable intake layer for client evidence and content operations.

sources.title: Langfuse v3 self-hosted architecture
sources.why_selected: Langfuse’s v3 discussion documents a stable self-hosted architecture path for observability workloads.
sources.usefulness: Use self-hosted traces when client data cannot leave the environment, while preserving evaluation and cost visibility.

sources.title: Self-Hosting Guide
sources.why_selected: A maintained practical guide aggregates deployment, storage, monitoring, and security choices across private infrastructure.
sources.usefulness: Use it as a checklist for a small Buildn lab rather than a shopping list of services.

sources.title: Plane on self-hosted project management
sources.why_selected: Plane connects self-hosting demand to upcoming SaaS data-use changes, making deployment choice a governance question as well as a cost question.
sources.usefulness: Frame project-system selection around data control, exportability, and operational burden.
